prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a parking lot collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1078; do not mention it.)
text:
This office represents the injured party in connection with the parking lot collision described in your insured's claim file. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, letter, or in person. Our client has suffered injuries that are still being evaluated by treating physicians, and we ask that any statements or requests be routed through counsel.

We also request a complete copy of the liability policy in force at the time of the incident, including declarations pages and all endorsements, along with written confirmation of the bodily injury and property damage limits available under that policy. Please also confirm whether any other coverage, such as an umbrella or excess policy, may apply.

Finally, we ask that your company preserve all evidence related to this loss. This includes photographs, dash camera or surveillance footage, vehicle data, adjuster notes, recorded statements, repair and appraisal records, and all communications with your insured. Please treat this letter as formal notice of the duty to preserve these materials.
